protocol.name: zt_environment_v1
protocol.copyright: SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later Copyright 2026 the ztOS authors

description.summary: where a window is: the phone or a desktop

protocol.description:
ztMETRO is two environments in one Wayland session: the phone (Metro's shell: one app at a time, full screen, touch, the on-screen keyboard) and a desktop (XFCE on a monitor or a virtual screen: stacking windows with frames, a pointer, a keyboard). A window can move from one to the other while it runs, with the same surface and the same process (ztmetro/desktop/DESIGN.md).
This protocol tells an app, for each of its toplevels, which one it is in, and tells it again every time the window moves, so that it can change its chrome and layout as it goes: frames and resizable windows on the desktop, the phone's full-screen layout on the phone.
An app without it can look at the toplevel's states: on the phone it is maximized and tiled on all four edges, on the desktop it is not. Or it can watch $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ztmetro-env/PID, which the shell keeps for every process with a window ("APP_ID phone|desktop OUTPUT" per window, rewritten when one moves).

interface.name: zt_environment_manager_v1

description.summary: gives each toplevel its environment object

interface.description: A global. One zt_environment_v1 per xdg_toplevel the client wants to know about.

description.summary: the manager goes; the objects it made stay

request.name: get_environment
request.description: The new object's first environment event comes with the toplevel's first configure (at once, if that configure has been sent already). Asking twice for the same toplevel is allowed; each object gets the events.

interface.name: zt_environment_v1
interface.description: Events about one toplevel. When the toplevel is destroyed, the object is inert: no more events; destroy it.

entry.name: phone
entry.summary: the phone's shell: full screen, one app in front

entry.name: desktop
entry.summary: a desktop: a window among others, framed and resizable

entry.name: touch
entry.summary: fingers on the screen the window is on

entry.name: pointer
entry.summary: a pointer (a mouse, or ztdesk's on the phone)

entry.name: keyboard
entry.summary: a keyboard with every key (not only the phone's)

event.name: environment

description.summary: the toplevel is in this environment now

event.description:
Sent first with the toplevel's first configure, then each time it moves, before the xdg_toplevel.configure that comes with the move (its new size and states). The client can apply both at that configure, in one frame.
output is the name of the wl_output the window is shown on (as wl_output.name gives it), or empty when it is shown on none.
